rows.title: NEAR Intents: Bridges
rows.summary: The NEAR Intents: Bridges program covers critical MPC and bridge infrastructure with Critical severity targets across smart contracts and network layers. KYC and a $5 POC fee are required to participate. Hotspots focus on threshold signature bypass, bridge relayer authorization, cross-chain replay, light-client proof validation, and MPC key disclosure—all directly tied to fund integrity and explicitly in-scope. Leads highlight duplicate-risk vectors in DKG manipulation, relayer validation, replay protection, proof verification, and TEE attestation, with high severity but low-to-medium duplicate probability.

gates.notes: KYC required, $5 POC submission fee, live program active

oos: Social engineering and physical TEE attacks
RNG quality issues without cross-asset impact

hotspots.title: MPC Threshold Signature Bypass
hotspots.why: Potential manipulation of DKG output or presignature validation could allow forging signatures below the required threshold, enabling unauthorized chain abstraction signatures.

hotspots.title: Omni Bridge Relayer Authorization Bypass
hotspots.why: Inadequate validation of relayer signatures against intent hashes may permit unauthorized asset withdrawal or double-spending across chains.

hotspots.title: Cross-Chain Intent Replay Attack
hotspots.why: Missing or weak replay nonces across intent domains could enable the same intent to be executed on multiple networks, resulting in double-spending.

hotspots.title: Bitcoin Light-Client Proof Validation Flaw
hotspots.why: Edge cases in Merkle proof verification for btc-light-client-contract may accept invalid Bitcoin block headers, leading to fund misdirection.

hotspots.title: MPC Key Share Information Disclosure
hotspots.why: Side-channel or network leakage of threshold key shares during DKG or signing phases could enable partial key reconstruction.

leads.title: MPC Threshold Signature Bypass via DKG Manipulation
leads.hypothesis: If DKG resharing parameters can be influenced by a subset of nodes, the effective threshold may be reduced, allowing signature forgery without full node compromise.
leads.why_not_oos: Directly impacts MPC network integrity and cross-chain signature validity; explicitly in-scope under cryptographic flaws and unauthorized access to MPC key shares.

leads.title: Bridge Relayer Signature Validation Gap
leads.hypothesis: Relayer signatures may not be fully verified against intent content hash, creating a window for malicious relayers to redirect cross-chain asset transfers.
leads.why_not_oos: Omni Bridge relayer logic is a core in-scope target for asset transfer security; findings fall under unauthorized transaction and bridge protocol execution flows.

leads.title: Cross-Chain Intent Replay Across Domains
leads.hypothesis: Intent identifiers may lack chain-binding or unique nonce mechanisms, allowing a valid intent submitted on one chain to be replayed and executed on another.
leads.why_not_oos: Replay attacks directly enable double-spending of funds across chains, covered under 'Cross-chain replay attacks enabling double-spending' in-scope category.

leads.title: Bitcoin Light-Client Merkle Proof Edge Cases
leads.hypothesis: Inconsistent validation logic for Bitcoin block Merkle proofs could accept fraudulent headers, causing the bridge to act on invalid Bitcoin state.
leads.why_not_oos: btc-light-client-contract is in-scope; proof validation flaws directly affect cross-chain asset backing and are explicitly listed as verification bypass targets.

leads.title: TEE Attestation Weakness in MPC Node Deployment
leads.hypothesis: If TEE attestation configuration is weakened or bypassed, MPC signing keys may be extracted or accepted outside the trusted execution environment, compromising the entire signing capability.
leads.why_not_oos: TEE integration is documented for MPC nodes; findings on attestation misconfiguration affect the 'Unauthorized access to MPC key shares or signing capability' in-scope category, even if TEE is in grace period.

rows.title: Bitmart Post-Incident Forensics Bounty Hunt
rows.summary: Bitmart Post-Incident Forensics Bounty Hunt is a paused forensic intelligence program seeking verified data on the December 2021 $196M hack involving stolen private keys across ETH, BSC, TRON, and VeChain. Attackers funneled funds through mixers like Tornado Cash, ChangeNOW, SimpleSwap, and Wasabi CoinJoin. The program offers bounties for attacker identification, fund flow tracing, and successful recovery, with additional percentages on recovered assets. Currently, the active contest is paused, and no triage or payouts are processing.

gates.notes: Program currently paused; active contest not running. Submissions accepted per guidelines but no active triage.

rows.payouts: $50-$58,000,000 bounty range per market price at incident date, plus 10%-30% of recovered funds as additional reward based on contribution significance. High-impact intelligence $1k-$5k, medium $500-$2k, low $50-$500.
scope: Attacker identification (on-chain & off-chain ties, social links, CEX account traces)
Transaction & fund flow analysis (on-chain tracing, mixing activity, laundering methods)
Infrastructure details (IP addresses, domains, hosting services used)
Other forensic evidence contributing to identifying the hacker(s)
oos: Repeating known data without new context
Activity violating laws or ethical standards

rows.title: BitDelta
rows.summary: BitDelta is an active HackenProof program with Web and apps scope, KYC mandatory, and a $1M maximum bounty across 163 submissions. Gates are clear: not private, not paused, fee zero, and no reputation barrier. Hotspots highlight IDOR, race conditions, and API rate-limiting as high-impact areas, while leads point to KYC bypass and CORS misconfiguration as out-of-scope-compliant investigation points.

gates.notes: KYC required (kyc:1); program active, not private/paused; mixed Web/apps scope; max bounty $1M; 163 submissions

kill: authorization_boundaries
input_sanitization
rate_limiting

hotspots.title: IDOR on User Asset Endpoints
hotspots.why: Missing access control checks allow unauthorized reading or modification of user balances and transaction history.

hotspots.title: Race Condition in Transaction Replay Handling
hotspots.why: Concurrent requests without proper nonce or locking mechanisms can enable double-spend or state inconsistency.

hotspots.title: Insufficient Rate Limiting on API Authentication
hotspots.why: Absence of progressive delays or account lockout facilitates automated brute-force or credential stuffing attacks.

leads.title: KYC Document Validation Bypass
leads.hypothesis: Weak MIME type or content validation on uploaded identity documents could allow forged submissions, enabling accounts without proper compliance checks.
leads.why_not_oos: KYC requirements are program-mandated (kyc:1); flaws directly subvert compliance and user trust.

leads.title: Overly Permissive CORS Policy
leads.hypothesis: Relaxed CORS headers across multiple origins may allow cross-domain data reading or request forgery in user browsers.
leads.why_not_oos: CORS configuration is part of the Web frontend scope and impacts data confidentiality.

rows.title: NEAR Protocol
rows.summary: The NEAR Protocol bug bounty program is currently paused, with KYC and a $5 POC fee acting as mandatory gates. In-scope targets are confined to the nearcore codebase and focus on critical blockchain issues such as fund theft, transaction manipulation, consensus and cryptographic flaws, with fixed $10k payouts for DoS fixes without hardfork. Out-of-scope includes network-level DoS, DoS/DDoS exploits, social engineering, spam, and any code outside nearcore. Due to the paused status, no active hunting or payouts are available at this time.

gates.notes: Program paused; KYC required; $5 POC fee required

scope: DoS issues fixed without hardfork (High severity, $10k fixed payout)

rows.title: Sui Protocol
rows.summary: Sui Protocol is an active, KYC/PoC-required bug bounty program on HackenProof with a $20 submission fee and million-dollar payout ceiling. The in-scope attack surface centers on Move/Rust smart contracts, bridge protocol, staking economics, consensus, and zkLogin, with Critical severity reserved for fund theft, BFT violations, and bridge message forgery. Hotspots identified focus on bridge forgery, consensus manipulation, zkLogin circuit integrity, storage rebate exploitation, and CLOB logic flaws, while leads explore staking incentive misalignment, authority reconfiguration front-running, package upgradeability, and gas griefing. No critical gates are red; all submissions must include working PoC and pass KYC.

gates.notes: KYC required, POC required, $20 antispam fee required; program Active, not private

rows.payouts: Payouts in USD or SUI token; Critical up to $1,000,000, High $500–$20,000, Medium $1,000–$5,000, Low $200–$1,000 per impact matrix
oos: web application XSS without fund impact

hotspots.title: Bridge Native Message Forgery Enabling >$3M Asset Theft
hotspots.why: Bridge contract message validation gaps could allow crafting malicious native bridge messages, enabling illegitimate minting or transfer of assets exceeding the $3M threshold with fully working PoC.

hotspots.title: Consensus BFT Assumption Violation via Epoch Stake Manipulation
hotspots.why: Manipulating delegated stake during epoch reconfiguration could grant authorities voting power vastly disproportionate (20x) to stake, compromising proof-of-stake governance integrity as per Critical impact criteria.

hotspots.title: zkLogin Circuit Construction Flaw Allowing Key Derivation Without Valid Identity
hotspots.why: Vulnerabilities in zkLogin circuit construction could permit deriving valid keys without satisfying on-chain identity policies, leading to unauthorized fund access or transaction signing.

hotspots.title: Move Contract Storage Rebate Exploitation After Epoch Change
hotspots.why: Edge cases in epoch-change transactions where excessive storage rebates on 0x5 object are not evenly distributed, allowing the first actor to touch the object to obtain rebates, causing proportional fund depreciation for other users.

hotspots.title: DeepBook v3 CLOB Logic Flaw Causing Permanent Fund Freeze
hotspots.why: Logic flaws in the CLOB order book could trigger invariant violations or unintended permanent freezing of funds, exceeding the known order-limit exclusion and causing significant loss or network disruption.

leads.title: Staking Reward Calculation Incentive Misalignment
leads.hypothesis: Edge cases in epoch reward distribution could allow attackers to claim disproportionate rewards by manipulating stake durations or epoch boundaries, beyond the minimum stake mitigation.
leads.why_not_oos: Directly affects SUI token holders and staking participants; impact falls within fund-related Critical/High categories.

leads.title: Authority Set Reconfiguration Front-Running
leads.hypothesis: Manipulating the stake delegation queue during epoch transitions could allow front-running of authority set changes, disproportionately benefiting specific authorities or attackers.
leads.why_not_oos: Impacts consensus governance and stake distribution, aligning with Critical impact category for BFT violation.

leads.title: Move Package Upgradeability Logic Flaw
leads.hypothesis: If Sui packages contain upgradeable logic without proper guards, attackers could upgrade contracts to extract funds, halt operations, or redirect state.
leads.why_not_oos: Affects smart contract logic and fund safety; in scope per smart_contract category and fund theft impacts.

leads.title: Gas Griefing via Excessive Parallel Contract Calls
leads.hypothesis: Crafting transaction bundles that maximize parallel gas usage could starve network resources or cause DoS for other users, though not direct fund theft.
leads.why_not_oos: Impacts network availability and user experience; medium severity but high EV if widespread across users.

rows.title: NEAR Smart Contracts
rows.summary: The NEAR Smart Contracts program on HackenProof scopes into critical core contracts (lockup, staking-pool, multisig, whitelist, staking-pool-factory, sputnik-dao) written in Rust/WASM. In-scope vulnerabilities center on fund theft, transaction manipulation, economic exploits, and governance flaws, with bounties up to $300k for Critical severity. Out-of-scope includes network-level DoS, social engineering, and spam, per program rules. Researchers must navigate KYC, POC requirements, and a $5 submission fee, with SLA triage within 5 business days.

gates.notes: KYC and POC required; $5 submission fee; program active

oos: network-level DoS unrelated to smart contract execution

hotspots.title: Lockup Vesting Schedule Manipulation
hotspots.why: Improper validation of start/end timestamps or owner transfer could allow premature fund release or schedule override, directly impacting fund integrity.

hotspots.title: Staking Pool Delegation Reward Theft
hotspots.why: Missing or insufficient checks on delegation messages could allow attackers to divert staking rewards by crafting malicious delegator calls, exploiting the pool's payout flow.

hotspots.title: Multisig Proposal Front-Running & Quorum Bypass
hotspots.why: Inadequate ordering or threshold validation in multisig could enable front-running of proposals or quorum manipulation, allowing unauthorized contract changes.

hotspots.title: Sputnik DAO Governance Bond Forgiveness Edge Case
hotspots.why: Flawed bonding or forgiveness period logic in DAO proposals could allow bond recovery without valid proposal execution, impacting DAO treasury integrity.

hotspots.title: Staking Pool Factory Parameter Validation Gap
hotspots.why: Insufficient input validation in factory deployment parameters could allow creation of malicious staking pools with exploitable withdrawal or reward logic.

hotspots.title: Unchecked Recursive Contract Calls in Staking Pool Execution
hotspots.why: Absence of call depth limits or gas metering in nested contract calls could enable griefing or state corruption during execution flows.

leads.title: Lockup Owner Transfer Bypass
leads.hypothesis: If lockup contract lacks proper owner change validation, attacker could transfer ownership and alter vesting terms exclusively through on-chain governance calls.
leads.why_not_oos: Entirely on-chain smart contract logic; no network-level DoS or external dependency.

leads.title: Staking Reward Rate Discrepancy
leads.hypothesis: Discrepancy between reward-per-share calculation and actual staked amount could allow inflated reward claims via crafted delegation messages.
leads.why_not_oos: Pure contract state manipulation; excluded from OOS scope.

leads.title: Multisig Threshold Arithmetic Flaw
leads.hypothesis: Incorrect threshold arithmetic could allow proposal approval with fewer signatures than required by the multisig configuration.
leads.why_not_oos: On-chain governance logic; does not involve network-level DoS or external attack surfaces.

leads.title: DAO Proposal Bond Refund Loophole
leads.hypothesis: Flawed bond refund logic could allow bond retrieval without valid proposal finalization, impacting DAO treasury economics.
leads.why_not_oos: Pure contract economic logic; no network-level DoS or social engineering involved.

leads.title: Cross-Contract Call Gas Forward Missing
leads.hypothesis: Missing gas forward in internal calls could cause callee failure and block legitimate execution flow, exploitable via repeated malicious call patterns.
leads.why_not_oos: Contract-internal gas metering; does not constitute network-level DoS or spam.

rows.title: NEAR Intents: Smart Contracts
rows.summary: NEAR Intents is an active HackenProof bug bounty program targeting the Verifier smart contract and associated atomic swap infrastructure on NEAR. Scope centers on fund security, transaction integrity, and cryptographic correctness in Rust/Wasm contracts, with Critical/High severity bugs rewarded up to $300,000. Key hotspot areas include intent signature validation, atomic execution ordering, and access control on fund withdrawals. Program requires KYC, a $5 submission fee, and payments in vested NEAR over 1 year; analysis gates are currently open (ok=true) with no critical showstoppers blocking participation.

gates.notes: KYC required; $5 submission fee; payment in NEAR vested over 1 year; test on private testnet encouraged

rows.payouts: Critical: up to $300,000; High: up to $100,000; Medium: up to $20,000; Low: up to $1,000; total High+Critical capped at 10% TVL or max severity budget
oos: network-level DoS unrelated to contract execution
impact on assets outside NEAR Intents ecosystem
kill: unbounded gas consumption
griefing without profit motive
network-level DoS unrelated to contract execution

hotspots.title: Inadequate Intent Signature Verification
hotspots.why: The execute_intents function may fail to properly validate BIP-322/TIP-191/ERC-191 signed payloads, allowing crafted intents to trigger unauthorized token transfers.

hotspots.title: Front-Running in Intent Execution Order
hotspots.why: Absence of commit-reveal or strict ordering mechanisms in execute_intents enables attackers to reorder intents via gas bidding, manipulating swap outcomes.

hotspots.title: Integer Overflow/Underflow in Balance Reconciliation
hotspots.why: Unsafe arithmetic or wrapping operations in balance calculations could allow amount manipulation beyond intended limits, leading to fund loss.

hotspots.title: Missing Access Control on Fund Withdrawal
hotspots.why: After atomic swap execution, anyone may be able to withdraw swapped funds without proof of correct intent fulfillment, leading to theft.

hotspots.title: Cryptographic Hash Collapse in Payload Processing
hotspots.why: Flawed hashing or signature recovery for external signing standards (BIP-322 etc.) could enable intent forgery and unauthorized transaction execution.

hotspots.title: Replay Attack Across Intent Executions
hotspots.why: Lack of nonce or session binding allows previously valid intents to be re-submitted and executed, potentially double-spending or altering allocations.

leads.title: Intent Replay Vulnerability
leads.hypothesis: Valid intents lacking replay protection can be resubmitted, enabling double-spending or allocation manipulation across multiple execution cycles.
leads.why_not_oos: Directly impacts transaction integrity and fund safety; falls within in-scope transaction manipulation criteria.

leads.title: Controller Privilege Escalation
leads.hypothesis: The contract upgrade/state migration interface (Controller) may lack robust admin checks, allowing unauthorized parameter changes or state overrides.
leads.why_not_oos: Affects long-term contract integrity and fund security; in-scope for protocol manipulation.

leads.title: PoA Bridge Token Representation Mismatch
leads.hypothesis: Discrepancies between PoA factory token contracts and Intents Verifier expectations could cause token misrouting or loss during cross-asset transfers.
leads.why_not_oos: Involves fund movement across assets; program explicitly covers price manipulation and fee payment bypass.

leads.title: Parameter Manipulation in Intent Creation
leads.hypothesis: Insufficient validation of intent parameters (amounts, asset types) during creation could allow out-of-range or malicious values to be processed later.
leads.why_not_oos: Leads to transaction manipulation and fee bypass; in-scope per program rules.

The program targets critical logic flaws, fund manipulation, and access control issues in-scope contracts, while out-of-scope excludes theoretical issues, compiler version gaps, and front-run-only vectors. Hotspots focus on unchecked transfers, admin privilege, arithmetic edge cases, reentrancy, intent replay, and upgradeability risks, with severity aligned to potential fund loss and recoverability.

gates.notes: KYC required; POC required; Move-on-Sui program; not private; active bounty range $10-$300k

Critical severity issues center on access control gaps, predictable nonce schemes, unbounded loops, fee manipulation, and missing circuit-breakers, all presenting direct risk to deposited assets.

rows.title: Account Abstraction Bugs
rows.summary: The Account Abstraction Bugs program on HackenProof targets ERC-4337 core smart contract logic in Solidity, with scope limited to core/utils folders and committed tags v0.6.0–v0.8.0. Critical severity bugs in EntryPoint validation, nonce management, and paymaster fee handling offer the highest bounties ($100k–$250k), while medium issues involve assumption inconsistencies and bounded-loop DOS. Gates require KYC, POC submission, and a $7 fee; the program is active and private=false. Hotspots and leads focus on validation bypass, stake censorship at O(1) cost, and nonce predictability, with duplicate reports likely high for nonce-related vectors.

gates.notes: KYC required, POC required, $7 submission fee, program active, private: false

scope: ERC-4337 EntryPoint contract validation and execution logic
Smart contract account (BaseAccount/SimpleAccount) authentication and signature verification
Paymaster operations including fee handling and gas payment logic
StakeManager deposit/stake management and reputation rules
NonceManager nonce generation, replay prevention, and settlement logic
Core and utils folders only, Solidity implementation bugs
oos: Network-level DoS attacks targeting specific bundlers, accounts, or paymasters
General libp2p or P2P layer attacks
Social engineering, phishing, or spam outside smart contract scope

hotspots.title: EntryPoint calldata validation gap allowing unintended call execution
hotspots.why: Insufficient checks on UserOperation calldata structure can permit execution of calls outside intended validation, potentially enabling fund theft or censorship.

hotspots.title: BaseAccount signature replay without strict nonce binding
hotspots.why: Absence of replay-proof mechanisms in _validateSignature permits resubmission of captured UserOps, disrupting account state or enabling double-spend conditions.

hotspots.title: Paymaster gas payment logic edge cases with token transfer semantics
hotspots.why: Improper handling of token transfer semantics (e.g., fee-on-transfer, rebasing tokens) in paymaster validation can cause undercharging, unexpected transfers, or transaction revert, affecting protocol economics.

hotspots.title: StakeManager parameter tweak enabling O(1) censorship of staked entities
hotspots.why: If reputation or stake adjustment parameters require minimal gas, an attacker can censor specific accounts at O(1) cost, violating protocol liveness and staked entity guarantees.

hotspots.title: Nonce derivation with insufficient entropy in UserOperation settlement
hotspots.why: Deterministic nonce generation without adequate randomness allows prediction of UserOp ordering, facilitating front-running or replay before bundler inclusion.

leads.title: Absence of emergency pause on EntryPoint/UserOperation critical paths
leads.hypothesis: Without a pause function, exploited vulnerabilities in UserOperation processing can persist, enabling ongoing fund disruption or mempool poisoning.
leads.why_not_oos: Pause mechanisms on core contract functions affecting liveness are in-scope for AA severity High, distinct from off-chain service outages.

leads.title: Stake management loops without gas cap causing transaction revert
leads.hypothesis: Loops over stake participant arrays can be forced to consume excessive gas, blocking legitimate stake operations and causing effective DOS of stake management.
leads.why_not_oos: Gas-griefing loops in core protocol logic are explicitly listed as in-scope DOS vectors against the AA protocol, not general bundler attacks.

leads.title: On-chain fee parameter manipulation via unvalidated governance inputs
leads.hypothesis: If fee adjustment parameters derived from governance are not validated on-chain, attackers can tilt economic incentives or extract excess fees from the protocol.
leads.why_not_oos: On-chain fee manipulation affecting protocol economics falls under AA in-scope bugs, distinct from off-chain governance attacks or specification gaps.

leads.title: State consistency gap between EntryPoint execution and account logic
leads.hypothesis: Discrepancies between assumed and actual states (e.g., balance vs. staked amount) during UserOp execution can enable unexpected token movements or replay.
leads.why_not_oos: Assumption inconsistencies within the AA core are explicitly recognized as in-scope severity Medium-High, separate from external contract bugs.

leads.title: Insufficient entropy in UserOperation nonce generation enabling ordering prediction
leads.hypothesis: Deterministic nonce generation without adequate randomness allows attackers to predict and manipulate UserOp ordering prior to bundler inclusion, compromising transaction fairness and mempool integrity.
leads.why_not_oos: Nonce predictability affecting AA mempool ordering is an in-scope vector; distinct from general external mempool front-running or unrelated attack vectors.

rows.title: Aptos Network
rows.summary: Aptos Network is an active Layer 1 bug bounty program on HackenProof, accepting Move and Rust smart contract audits with KYC, POC, and a $100 submission fee. Bounties range from $0 to $250,000 based on severity, with Critical rewards for fund-loss or consensus vulnerabilities. Hotspots identified focus on governance parameter validation, pause mechanism gaps, nonce predictability in Account Abstraction, unbounded loops, and Permissioned Signer privilege escalation, all within in-scope targets and not flagged as out-of-scope or known issues.

gates.notes: KYC required; POC required; $100 submission fee; program active and not private

rows.payouts: Critical: up to $250,000; High: up to $50,000; Medium: up to $10,000; Low: $0 per program severity mapping.

hotspots.title: Unvalidated governance parameter in Move fee calculation enabling fund diversion
hotspots.why: Governance-updated Move module parameters lack input bounds checks; attacker could manipulate fees or enable unauthorized minting, directly impacting user funds without requiring a hardfork.

hotspots.title: Missing emergency pause on critical Move module transfers
hotspots.why: Critical transfer and withdrawal functions lack an emergency pause mechanism; the gap is a patchable configuration (not hardfork-required), and exploitation could enable fund diversion matching program Critical severity for loss-of-funds vectors.

hotspots.title: Predictable nonce derivation in AIP-104 Account Abstraction enabling front-run
hotspots.why: If nonce generation in AIP-104 lacks sufficient entropy, attackers predict transaction ordering, front-run intents, and extract value from user accounts.

hotspots.title: Unbounded loop in Move reward distribution without gas cap
hotspots.why: Reward/distribution loops iterate over user sets without gas limits; per program rules, DoS fixable without hardfork falls into Medium severity, but impact on user funds elevates concern beyond trivial.

leads.hypothesis: Governance proposals that update fee or transfer module parameters lack input bounds checking, allowing parameter drift that diverts funds or enables minting.
leads.why_not_oos: Governance-upgraded parameters directly affect network operations and user funds; program explicitly includes loss-of-funds vulnerabilities in scope and rewards them based on severity classification.

leads.title: Absence of pause on critical withdrawal paths in Move modules
leads.hypothesis: Critical transfer/withdrawal functions lack an emergency pause flag, preventing recovery during active exploits and matching the program's Critical severity for permanent freezing of funds (where fix is patchable without hardfork).
leads.why_not_oos: Program rules accept Medium DoS without hardfork, but absence of pause on fund-moving functions is distinct and in scope for Critical rewards when patchable.

leads.title: Predictable sequence numbers in Aptos transaction pool enabling front-run
leads.hypothesis: Transaction sequence derivation in the Move transaction pool lacks cryptographic randomness, allowing attackers to front-run high-value transfers or governance calls.
leads.why_not_oos: Front-running of user transactions impacts fund integrity and is not a pure network DoS; program includes loss-of-funds vectors in scope.

rows.title: DeltaPrime Smart Contracts
rows.summary: DeltaPrime is an active Solidity-based lending bug bounty program on HackenProof, focusing on undercollateralized loan protocols via Prime Accounts and Pool contracts. The in-scope target is v1.1.0 contracts with Critical severity priority, while v2 auxiliary contracts are out of scope. Hotspots center on oracle-mediated solvency manipulation, reentrancy in withdrawal paths, missing pause mechanisms, governance parameter injection, and gas-exhaustive loops. Leads extend these into fee-on-transfer token handling, predictable account creation, admin fee validation, and cross-component state consistency gaps, with duplicate probability adjusted against the program's 510 prior submissions.

rows.title: Cronos zkEVM Smart Contracts
rows.summary: Cronos zkEVM Smart Contracts is an active EVM/Solidity-focused bug bounty covering Amply Finance, H2 Finance, and Fulcrom DeFi protocols, with an emphasis on vulnerabilities causing unintentional fund withdrawal or user asset loss.
